       The three tags below fire real, billable hits wherever the page is
       served, which meant `npm run preview` and the GitHub Pages mirror were
       sending pageviews, Meta signals with domain=localhost, and Google Ads
       audience pings into the live properties — inflating the numbers with
       traffic that is us. It also keeps the browser's loading indicator
       spinning long after the content has painted, because these requests are
       still in flight, which reads as "the page never finishes loading".
       Only the production hostnames count. Everything else gets no tags at
       all, so local previews are silent and fast.
       WHEN they run is decided here too. Measured on the live site: Meta Pixel
       and Bing UET cost 13 Lighthouse points and 816ms of main-thread blocking
       — more than every Google tag combined — because ~214 KB of script parses
       and executes while the visitor is trying to read and tap.
       So they now wait for the first interaction instead of firing during
       load. The obvious objection to deferring is losing the visitor who never
       interacts, which is why there is also a fallback timer: anyone still on
       the page after it elapses is counted anyway. The only visitor missed is
       one who leaves within that window without scrolling, tapping or typing —
       already a bounce by any measure. A `scroll` counts, so on a page this
       tall almost everyone qualifies within a second or two. --><script></script><!-- No Google tag here on purpose.

       was counted twice in GA4, and the browser downloaded ~186 KB of gtag.js

       off in the Cloudflare dashboard, Analytics and Ads stop with it and this
       snippet has to come back.
